title: Shortest Subarray With OR at Least K I
description:
You are given an array `nums` of non-negative integers and an integer `k`.

An array is called special if the bitwise OR of all of its elements is at least `k`.

Return the length of the shortest special non-empty subarray of `nums`, or return -1 if no special subarray exists.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 50
0 <= nums[i] <= 50
0 <= k < 64

test_cases.explanation: Subarray [2] has bitwise OR equal to 2 >= 2, length is 1.
Subarray [2, 1, 8] has bitwise OR equal to 11 >= 10, length is 3.

title: Replace All ?'s to Avoid Consecutive Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string `s` containing only lowercase English letters and the '?' character, convert all the '?' characters into lowercase English letters such that the final string does not contain any consecutive repeating characters.

You cannot modify the non-'?' characters.

It is guaranteed that there are no consecutive repeating characters in the given string except for '?'.

Return the final string after all the conversions (any valid string will be accepted).

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 100
s consists of lowercase English letters and '?'.

test_cases.explanation: Replacing '?' with 'a' gives 'azs' where no two adjacent characters are repeating.
Replacing '?' with 'a' gives 'ubvaw'.

title: Rearrange Spaces Between Words
description:
You are given a string `text` of words that are separated by one or more spaces. Each word consists of lowercase English letters and at least one word exists.

Rearrange the spaces so that there is an equal number of spaces between every pair of adjacent words that is maximized. If you cannot distribute all the spaces equally, place the extra spaces at the end of the string.

Return the string after rearranging the spaces.

### Constraints
1 <= text.length <= 100
text consists of lowercase English letters and spaces ' '.
text contains at least one word.

test_cases.explanation: Total 9 spaces and 4 words. Distribute 9 // 3 = 3 spaces between words, 0 extra.
Total 7 spaces and 3 words. 3 spaces between words, 1 extra at the end.

title: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
description:
There are `n` available seats and `n` students in a room. You are given an array `seats` of length `n`, where `seats[i]` is the position of the `i`-th seat. You are also given the array `students` of length `n`, where `students[j]` is the position of the `j`-th student.

You may perform the following move any number of times: increase or decrease the position of the `i`-th student by 1.

Return the minimum number of moves required to move each student to a seat such that no two students are in the same seat.

### Constraints
n == seats.length == students.length
1 <= n <= 100
1 <= seats[i], students[j] <= 100

test_cases.explanation: Sorted seats [1, 3, 5], sorted students [2, 4, 7]. Total moves: |1-2| + |3-4| + |5-7| = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.
Total moves needed is 7.

title: Powerful Integers
description:
Given three integers `x`, `y`, and `bound`, return a list of all the powerful integers that have a value less than or equal to `bound`.

An integer is powerful if it can be written as `x^i + y^j` for some integers `i >= 0` and `j >= 0`.

Return the answer in sorted order.

### Constraints
1 <= x, y <= 100
0 <= bound <= 10^6

test_cases.explanation: Powerful integers <= 10 are 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10.
Powerful integers <= 15 are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14.

title: Find Winner on a Tic Tac Toe Game
description:
Tic-tac-toe is played by two players A and B on a 3 x 3 grid. Players alternate placing 'X' (for A) and 'O' (for B). A player wins if they place three of their marks in a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal row.

Given a 2D integer array `moves` representing the sequence of moves made, return the winner ("A" or "B") if there is one, "Draw" if the grid is full with no winner, or "Pending" if the game is still ongoing.

### Constraints
1 <= moves.length <= 9
moves[i].length == 2
0 <= row_i, col_i <= 2
There are no repeated elements on moves.

test_cases.explanation: A wins as they make 3 in a row diagonally.
B wins on column 0.

title: Fair Candy Swap
description:
Alice and Bob have different amounts of candy. You are given two integer arrays `aliceSizes` and `bobSizes` where `aliceSizes[i]` is the size of the `i`-th box of candy Alice has and `bobSizes[j]` is the size of the `j`-th box of candy Bob has.

Since they are friends and want to share fairly, they would like to exchange one candy box each so that both have the same total amount of candy.

Return an integer array `[x, y]` where `x` is the size of the candy box Alice must exchange and `y` is the size of the candy box Bob must exchange. If multiple answers exist, return any.

### Constraints
1 <= aliceSizes.length, bobSizes.length <= 10^4
1 <= aliceSizes[i], bobSizes[j] <= 10^5
Alice and Bob have different total amounts of candy.
There will be at least one valid answer.

test_cases.explanation: Alice trades 1 for 2, both will have 2 candies.
Alice trades 1 for 2, both will have 3 candies.

title: Number of Different Integers in a String
description:
You are given a string `word` that consists of digits and lowercase English letters.

You will replace every non-digit character with a space. For example, `"a123bc34d8ef34"` becomes `" 123  34 8  34"`. Notice that remaining integers are separated by at least one space: `"123"`, `"34"`, `"8"`, and `"34"`.

Return the number of different integers after performing the replacement operations on `word`.

Two integers are considered different if their decimal representations without any leading zeros are different.

### Constraints
1 <= word.length <= 1000
word consists of digits and lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Different integers are 123, 34, 8. Count is 3.
Different integers are 1234 and 234. Count is 2.

title: Reformat Phone Number
description:
You are given a phone number as a string `number`. `number` consists of digits, spaces `' '`, and/or dashes `'-'`.

You would like to reformat the phone number in a certain manner:
- Remove all spaces and dashes.
- Group the digits from left to right into blocks of length 3 until there are 4 or fewer digits remaining.
- The final digits are then grouped as follows:
  - 2 digits: A single block of length 2.
  - 3 digits: A single block of length 3.
  - 4 digits: Two blocks of length 2 each.

Return the formatted phone number.

### Constraints
2 <= number.length <= 100
number consists of digits and the characters '-' and ' '.
There are at least two digits in number.

test_cases.explanation: Digits are '123456'. Form 2 blocks of 3: '123-456'.
Digits are '1234567'. Form '123' then 4 digits split into 2-2: '123-45-67'.

title: Fixed Point
description:
Given an array of distinct integers `arr` sorted in ascending order, return the smallest index `i` that satisfies `arr[i] == i`. If no such index exists, return -1.

### Constraints
1 <= arr.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
arr is strictly increasing.

test_cases.explanation: arr[3] = 3 is the smallest index where arr[i] == i.
arr[0] = 0 is the smallest fixed point.

title: Convert 1D Array Into 2D Array
description:
You are given a 0-indexed 1D integer array `original` and two integers `m` and `n`. You are tasked with creating a 2D array with `m` rows and `n` columns using all the elements from `original`.

The elements from indices `0` to `n - 1` (inclusive) of `original` should form the first row of the constructed 2D array, the elements from indices `n` to `2 * n - 1` should form the second row, and so on.

Return an `m x n` 2D array constructed according to the above procedure, or an empty 2D array if it is impossible.

### Constraints
1 <= original.length <= 5 * 10^4
1 <= original[i] <= 10^5
1 <= m, n <= 4 * 10^4

test_cases.explanation: The constructed 2D array is [[1, 2], [3, 4]].
Constructed 2D array is [[1, 2, 3]].

title: Get Maximum in Generated Array
description:
You are given an integer `n`. An array `nums` of length `n + 1` is generated in the following way:
- `nums[0] = 0`
- `nums[1] = 1`
- `nums[2 * i] = nums[i]` when `2 <= 2 * i <= n`
- `nums[2 * i + 1] = nums[i] + nums[i + 1]` when `2 <= 2 * i + 1 <= n`

Return the maximum integer in the array `nums`.

### Constraints
0 <= n <= 100

test_cases.explanation: nums generated: [0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3]. Maximum value is 3.
nums: [0, 1, 1]. Maximum value is 1.

title: Verifying an Alien Dictionary
description:
In an alien language, surprisingly, they also use English lowercase letters, but possibly in a different `order`. The `order` of the alphabet is some permutation of lowercase letters.

Given a sequence of `words` written in the alien language, and the `order` of the alphabet, return `true` if and only if the given `words` are sorted lexicographically in this alien language.

### Constraints
1 <= words.length <= 100
1 <= words[i].length <= 20
order.length == 26
All characters in words[i] and order are English lowercase letters.

test_cases.explanation: 'h' comes before 'l' in the alien alphabet, so the order is valid.
'world' comes before 'word' in this order, but 'word' appears first in words. Return false.

title: Smallest Range I
description:
You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.

In one operation, you can choose any index `i` where `0 <= i < nums.length` and change `nums[i]` to `nums[i] + x` where `x` is an integer from `[-k, k]`. You can apply this operation at most once for each index `i`.

The score of `nums` is the difference between the maximum and minimum elements in `nums`.

Return the minimum score of `nums` after applying the mentioned operation at most once for each index.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
0 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
0 <= k <= 10^4

test_cases.explanation: The score is max(nums) - min(nums) = 1 - 1 = 0.
Change to [2, 8]. Score is 8 - 2 = 6.

title: Most Frequent Number Following Key In an Array
description:
You are given a 0-indexed integer array `nums`. You are also given an integer `key`, which is present in `nums`.

For every unique integer `target` in `nums`, count the number of times `target` immediately follows an occurrence of `key` in `nums`.

Return the `target` with the maximum count. The test cases are generated such that the `target` with maximum count is unique.

### Constraints
2 <= nums.length <= 1000
1 <= nums[i], key <= 1000
At least one target follows key in nums.

test_cases.explanation: For target = 100, there are 2 occurrences at index 1 and 4 following key = 1. Return 100.
Target 2 follows key 2 three times. Output 2.

title: Minimum Subsequence in Non-Increasing Order
description:
Given the array `nums`, obtain a subsequence of the array whose sum of elements is strictly greater than the sum of the non-included elements.

If there are multiple solutions, return the subsequence with minimum size and if there still exist multiple solutions, return the subsequence with the maximum total sum of all its elements. A subsequence of an array can be obtained by erasing some (possibly zero) elements from the array.

Return the solution sorted in non-increasing order.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 500
1 <= nums[i] <= 100

test_cases.explanation: The subsequence [10, 9] has sum 19, which is strictly greater than the sum of the remaining elements (4 + 3 + 8 = 15).
Subsequence [7, 7, 6] has sum 20 > 8.

title: Distribute Candies to People
description:
We distribute some number of `candies`, to a row of `n = num_people` people in the following way:

We then give 1 candy to the first person, 2 candies to the second person, and so on until we give `n` candies to the last person.

Then, we go back to the start of the row, giving `n + 1` candies to the first person, `n + 2` candies to the second person, and so on until we give `2 * n` candies to the last person.

This process continues until we run out of candies. The last person will receive all of our remaining candies.

Return an array of length `num_people` that represents the final distribution of candies.

### Constraints
1 <= candies <= 10^9
1 <= num_people <= 1000

test_cases.explanation: Round 1: [1, 2, 3, 1]. Total candies = 7.
Candies distribution: [5, 2, 3].

title: Check if Strings Can be Made Equal With Operations I
description:
You are given two strings `s1` and `s2`, both of length 4, consisting of lowercase English letters.

You can apply the following operation on any of the two strings any number of times: choose two indices `i` and `j` such that `j - i = 2` and swap the two characters at those indices in the string.

Return `true` if you can make the strings `s1` and `s2` equal, and `false` otherwise.

### Constraints
s1.length == s2.length == 4
s1 and s2 consist only of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Swap characters at 0 and 2 ('cbad'), then 1 and 3 ('cdab'). Equals s2.
Cannot make s1 equal to s2, return false.

title: Convert Integer to the Sum of Two No-Zero Integers
description:
No-Zero integer is a positive integer that does not contain any '0' in its decimal representation.

Given an integer `n`, return a list of two integers `[A, B]` where:
- `A` and `B` are No-Zero integers.
- `A + B = n`

The test cases are generated so that there is at least one valid solution. If there are many valid solutions, you can return any of them.

### Constraints
2 <= n <= 10^4

test_cases.explanation: A = 1, B = 1. A + B = 2 and neither contains '0'.
A = 2, B = 9. A + B = 11 and neither contains '0'.

title: Occurrences After Bigram
description:
Given two strings `first` and `second`, consider occurrences in some text of the form `"first second third"`, where `second` comes immediately after `first`, and `third` comes immediately after `second`.

Return an array of all the words `third` for each occurrence of `"first second third"`.

### Constraints
1 <= text.length <= 1000
text consists of lowercase English letters and spaces.
All the words in text are separated by a single space.
1 <= first.length, second.length <= 10
first and second consist of lowercase English letters.

inputs.text: alice is a good girl she is a good student

test_cases.explanation: 'good' followed by 'girl' and 'student'. Return ['girl', 'student'].

inputs.text: we will we will rock you

test_cases.explanation: 'we will' followed by 'we' and 'rock'. Return ['we', 'rock'].

title: Long Pressed Name
description:
Your friend is typing his `name` into a keyboard. Sometimes, when typing a character `c`, the key might get long pressed, and the character will be typed 1 or more times.

You examine the `typed` characters of the keyboard. Return `true` if it is possible that it was your friends name, with some characters (possibly none) being long pressed.

### Constraints
1 <= name.length, typed.length <= 1000
name and typed consist of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: 'a' and 'e' in 'alex' were long pressed.
'e' was only typed once instead of twice in 'saeed'.

title: Latest Time by Replacing Hidden Digits
description:
You are given a string `time` in the form of `"hh:mm"`, where some of the digits in the string are hidden (represented by `?`).

The valid times are those inclusively between `"00:00"` and `"23:59"`.

Return the latest valid time you can get from `time` by replacing the hidden digits.

### Constraints
time is in the format "hh:mm".
It is guaranteed that you can produce a valid time from the given string.

test_cases.explanation: The latest valid time is '23:50'.
The latest valid time is '09:39'.

title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
description:
A shop is offering a discount: for every two candies you buy, you get a third candy for free.

You can choose any candy that has a cost less than or equal to the minimum cost of the two candies you bought.

Given an integer array `cost` where `cost[i]` is the cost of the `i`-th candy, return the minimum cost of buying all the candies.

### Constraints
1 <= cost.length <= 100
1 <= cost[i] <= 100

test_cases.explanation: Buy 3 and 2, get 1 for free. Total cost = 5.
Buy 9, 7 (get 6 free), buy 5, 2 (get 2 free). Total = 9 + 7 + 5 + 2 = 23.

title: Find Nearest Point That Has the Same X or Y Coordinate
description:
You are given two integers, `x` and `y`, which represent your current location on a Cartesian grid: `(x, y)`.

You are also given an array `points` where each `points[i] = [a_i, b_i]` represents that a point exists at `(a_i, b_i)`. A point is valid if it shares the same x-coordinate or the same y-coordinate as your location.

Return the index (0-indexed) of the valid point with the smallest Manhattan distance from your current location. If there are multiple, return the smallest index. If there are no valid points, return -1.

### Constraints
1 <= points.length <= 10^4
points[i].length == 2
1 <= x, y, points[i][0], points[i][1] <= 10^4

test_cases.explanation: Valid points: [3,1] (dist 3), [2,4] (dist 1), [4,4] (dist 1). Smallest index with dist 1 is index 2.
Point (3, 4) is at distance 0, return index 0.

title: Uncommon Words from Two Sentences
description:
A sentence is a string of single-space separated words where each word consists only of lowercase letters.

A word is uncommon if it appears exactly once in one of the sentences, and does not appear in the other sentence.

Given two sentences `s1` and `s2`, return a list of all the uncommon words in sorted order.

### Constraints
1 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 200
s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters and spaces.
s1 and s2 do not have leading or trailing spaces.
All the words in s1 and s2 are separated by a single space.

test_cases.explanation: 'sweet' and 'sour' appear exactly once in total.
'banana' appears once, 'apple' appears twice. Return ['banana'].

title: Intersection of Three Sorted Arrays
description:
Given three integer arrays `arr1`, `arr2` and `arr3` sorted in strictly increasing order, return a sorted array of only the integers that appeared in all three arrays.

### Constraints
1 <= arr1.length, arr2.length, arr3.length <= 1000
1 <= arr1[i], arr2[i], arr3[i] <= 2000
arr1, arr2, and arr3 are strictly increasing.

test_cases.explanation: Common elements are 1 and 5.
No common elements, return [].

title: Sum of Digits in the Minimum Number
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the minimum element in `nums`.

Let `S` be the sum of the digits of the minimum element.

Return 0 if `S` is odd, and 1 if `S` is even.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 100
1 <= nums[i] <= 100

test_cases.explanation: Minimum element is 1. Sum of digits is 1, which is odd, so return 0.
Minimum is 33. Sum of digits is 3 + 3 = 6 (even), so return 1.

title: Cells in a Range on an Excel Sheet
description:
A cell `(r, c)` of an excel sheet is represented as a string `"<col><row>"` where:
- `<col>` denotes the column number of the cell. It is represented by uppercase English letters (A through Z).
- `<row>` is the row number of the cell.

You are given a string `s` in the format `"<col1><row1>:<col2><row2>"` representing a range of cells.

Return the list of cells `(r, c)` in the range, sorted in non-decreasing order first by columns and then by rows.

### Constraints
s.length == 5
'A' <= s[0] <= s[3] <= 'Z'
'1' <= s[1] <= s[4] <= '9'

test_cases.explanation: Cells in column-major order: ['K1', 'K2', 'L1', 'L2'].

title: Positions of Large Groups
description:
In a string `s` of lowercase letters, these letters form consecutive groups of the same character.

For example, a string like `s = "abbxxxxzyy"` has the groups `"a"`, `"bb"`, `"xxxx"`, `"z"`, and `"yy"`.

A group is identified by an interval `[start, end]`, where `start` and `end` denote the start and end-indices (inclusive) of the group.

We call a group large if it has 3 or more characters.

Return the intervals of every large group sorted in increasing order by start index.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains lowercase English letters only.

test_cases.explanation: 'xxxx' has 4 letters starting at index 3 and ending at index 6. Output [[3, 6]].
No large groups, return [].

title: Check If a Number Is Majority Element in a Sorted Array
description:
Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer `target`, return `true` if `target` is a majority element, or `false` otherwise.

A majority element in an array `nums` is an element that appears more than `nums.length / 2` times in the array.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 1000
1 <= nums[i], target <= 10^9
nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

test_cases.explanation: The value 5 appears 5 times and the length of the array is 9. 5 > 9/2, so return true.
101 appears 2 times, which is not > 4/2. Return false.

title: Maximum Number of Visible Points
description:
You are given an array `points`, an integer `angle`, and your `location`, where `location = [pos_x, pos_y]` and `points[i] = [x_i, y_i]` both denote integral coordinates on the X-Y plane.

Initially, you are facing such that you can see all points within your field of view of `angle` degrees. You can view all points directly on your location regardless of orientation.

Return the maximum number of points you can view at once.

### Constraints
1 <= points.length <= 10^5
points[i].length == 2
location.length == 2
0 <= angle <= 360
0 <= pos_x, pos_y, xi, yi <= 100

test_cases.explanation: All 3 points can be visible within a 90 degree field of view.
Point at [1,1] is always visible, plus 3 other points: total 4.

title: Add Edges to Make Degrees of All Nodes Even
description:
There is an undirected graph consisting of `n` nodes numbered from 1 to `n`. You are given an integer `n` and a 2D integer array `edges` where `edges[i] = [a_i, b_i]`.

You can add at most two additional edges (possibly zero) between any two nodes that do not already have an edge between them.

Return `true` if it is possible to make the degree of each node in the graph even, or `false` otherwise.

### Constraints
2 <= n <= 10^5
1 <= edges.length <= 10^5
edges[i].length == 2
1 <= ui, vi <= n
ui != vi
There are no repeated edges.

test_cases.explanation: Add edges (1, 5) and (3, 5) to make all node degrees even.
Add edges (1, 3) and (2, 4) to make all node degrees even.

title: Snakes and Ladders
description:
You are given an `n x n` integer matrix `board` where cells are labeled from 1 to `n^2` in Boustrophedon style from the bottom left.

You start on square 1. In each move, from square `curr`, choose a destination square `next` with label in the range `[curr + 1, min(curr + 6, n^2)]`. If `next` has a snake or ladder (represented by a positive value), you must move to the destination of that snake or ladder.

Return the least number of moves required to reach square `n^2`. If it is not possible, return -1.

### Constraints
n == board.length == board[i].length
2 <= n <= 20
grid_val is -1 or between 1 and n^2
The squares labeled 1 and n^2 do not have any ladders or snakes.

test_cases.explanation: In 4 moves, reach the destination square 36.
Roll 1 to square 2 and take ladder to 3, then roll 1 to square 4. Total = 1 move.

title: Minimum Number of Flips to Make the Binary String Alternating
description:
You are given a binary string `s`. You are allowed to perform two types of operations on `s` in any order:
- Type-1: Remove the first character of the string and append it to the end of the string.
- Type-2: Pick any character in `s` and flip its value.

Return the minimum number of type-2 operations you need to make `s` alternating.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
s[i] is either '0' or '1'.

test_cases.explanation: Rotate string to '011100', then flip 2 characters to achieve alternating string '010101'.
The string is already alternating, return 0.

title: Sum Game
description:
Alice and Bob play a game. You are given a string `num` of even length consisting of digits and `?`.

In each turn, a player picks a `?` and replaces it with any digit from '0' to '9'. Alice goes first. The game ends when all `?` are replaced.

Bob wins if the sum of the first half of digits equals the sum of the second half of digits. Alice wins otherwise.

Return `true` if Alice wins, or `false` if Bob wins.

### Constraints
2 <= num.length <= 10^5
num.length is even.
num consists of digits and '?'.

test_cases.explanation: Left sum = 5, right sum = 5. No '?' remaining, Bob wins, Alice loses (return false).
Alice can always make the sum unequal, so Alice wins (return true).

title: Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid
description:
You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array `grid` of size `3 x 3`, representing the number of stones next to each cell. The total number of stones is 9.

In one move, you can place a stone from a cell to any of its four adjacent neighboring cells.

Return the minimum number of moves required to place one stone in each cell.

### Constraints
grid.length == grid[i].length == 3
0 <= grid[i][j] <= 9
Sum of all grid[i][j] == 9

test_cases.explanation: Move one stone from (2,1) to (0,2). Manhattan distance = |2-0| + |1-2| = 3 moves.
Requires 4 moves to spread all stones to every cell.

title: Stone Game VI
description:
Alice and Bob take turns playing a game, with Alice going first.

There are `n` stones. In each turn, a player removes a stone from the pile and adds the stone's value to their score. Alice and Bob value stones differently: Alice values the `i`-th stone as `aliceValues[i]`, and Bob values it as `bobValues[i]`.

Return 1 if Alice wins, -1 if Bob wins, or 0 if they draw.

### Constraints
n == aliceValues.length == bobValues.length
1 <= n <= 10^5
1 <= aliceValues[i], bobValues[i] <= 100

test_cases.explanation: Alice takes stone 1 (value 3). Bob takes stone 0 (value 2). Alice has 3, Bob has 2. Alice wins (return 1).
Alice takes stone 1 (2). Bob takes stone 0 (3). Draw (return 0).

title: Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the Tasks
description:
There are `n` tasks assigned to you. The task times are represented as an integer array `tasks` of length `n`, where the `i`-th task takes `tasks[i]` hours to finish. A work session is at most `sessionTime` hours long.

You cannot work on two tasks simultaneously. You can finish tasks in any order.

Return the minimum number of work sessions needed to finish all the tasks.

### Constraints
1 <= tasks.length <= 14
1 <= tasks[i] <= sessionTime <= 15

test_cases.explanation: Session 1: [1, 2], Session 2: [3]. Total 2 sessions.
All tasks can be finished in 1 session of duration 8.

title: Three Equal Parts
description:
You are given an array `arr` which consists of only zeros and ones, divide the array into three non-empty parts such that all of these parts represent the same binary value.

If it is possible, return any `[i, j]` with `i + 1 < j`, such that `arr[0..i]`, `arr[i+1..j-1]`, and `arr[j..arr.length-1]` represent the same binary value. If it is not possible, return `[-1, -1]`.

### Constraints
3 <= arr.length <= 3 * 10^4
arr[i] is 0 or 1

test_cases.explanation: [1], [0, 1], [0, 1] represent binary 1. Output [0, 3].
Not possible to divide into three equal binary parts, return [-1, -1].

title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Applying Operations
description:
You are given a string `s` of even length consisting of digits from 0 to 9, and two integers `a` and `b`.

You can apply either of the following two operations any number of times:
- Add `a` to all odd indices of `s` (modulo 10).
- Rotate `s` to the right by `b` positions.

Return the lexicographically smallest string you can obtain by applying the above operations any number of times.

### Constraints
2 <= s.length <= 100
s.length is even.
s consists of digits from '0' to '9' only.
1 <= a <= 9
1 <= b <= s.length - 1

test_cases.explanation: Applying rotate and add operations yields smallest string '2050'.
Lexicographically smallest string achievable is '24'.

title: Minimum Area Rectangle II
description:
You are given an array of points in the X-Y plane `points` where `points[i] = [x_i, y_i]`.

Return the minimum area of any rectangle formed from these points, with sides not necessarily parallel to the X and Y axes. If there is not any such rectangle, return 0.

### Constraints
1 <= points.length <= 500
points[i].length == 2
0 <= xi, yi <= 4 * 10^4
All the given points are unique.

test_cases.explanation: The 4 points form a rectangle with area 2.0.
Points [1,0],[2,0],[2,1],[1,1] form a rectangle of area 1.0.

title: Pyramid Transition Matrix
description:
You are stacking blocks to form a pyramid. Each block has a single color, which is represented by a single letter. Each row of blocks has one less block than the row below it and is centered on top.

To build a block of color `C` on top of adjacent blocks of color `A` and `B`, the triangular pattern `ABC` must be among the `allowed` patterns.

Given the bottom row `bottom` and list of `allowed` patterns, return `true` if you can build the pyramid all the way to the top, or `false` otherwise.

### Constraints
bottom.length in [2, 6]
allowed.length in [1, 216]
allowed[i].length == 3
Letters are among 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G'

test_cases.explanation: Allowed blocks allow building a pyramid up to the apex.
Cannot reach the top of the pyramid, return false.

title: Minimum Number of People to Teach
description:
On a social network, there are `n` languages numbered 1 through `n` and users who speak them.

You are given an array `languages` where `languages[i]` is the set of languages the `(i + 1)`-th user speaks, and a 2D array `friendships` where `friendships[j] = [u_j, v_j]` denotes a friendship between user `u_j` and user `v_j`.

You can choose one language and teach it to some users so that all friends can communicate with each other.

Return the minimum number of users you need to teach.

### Constraints
2 <= n <= 500
1 <= languages.length <= 500
1 <= languages[i].length <= n
1 <= friendships.length <= 500
friendships[i].length == 2
1 <= ui, vi <= languages.length
ui != vi

test_cases.explanation: Teach language 1 to user 2. Then all friends can communicate (1 user taught).
Teach language 3 to users 1 and 3 (2 users taught).

title: Process Tasks Using Servers
description:
You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays `servers` and `tasks` of lengths `n` and `m` respectively. `servers[i]` is the weight of the `i`-th server, and `tasks[j]` is the time needed to process the `j`-th task.

Tasks are assigned to the available server with the smallest weight, breaking ties with the smallest server index.

Return an array `ans` of length `m`, where `ans[j]` is the index of the server the `j`-th task will be assigned to.

### Constraints
servers.length == n
tasks.length == m
1 <= n, m <= 2 * 10^5
1 <= servers[i], tasks[j] <= 2 * 10^5

test_cases.explanation: Servers assigned: [2, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2].
Servers assigned: [1, 4, 1, 4, 1, 3, 2].

title: Avoid Flood in The City
description:
Your country has an infinite number of lakes. Initially, all the lakes are empty, but when it rains over the `n`-th lake, the `n`-th lake becomes full of water. If it rains over a lake that is full of water, there will be a flood.

You are given an integer array `rains` where `rains[i] > 0` means it will rain over lake `rains[i]`, and `rains[i] == 0` means there is no rain and you can dry one lake.

Return an array `ans` where `ans[i] == -1` if `rains[i] > 0`, and `ans[i]` is the lake you dried if `rains[i] == 0`. If it is impossible to avoid flood, return an empty array.

### Constraints
1 <= rains.length <= 10^5
0 <= rains[i] <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: No dry days, no flood occurs: [-1, -1, -1, -1].
Dry lake 2 then lake 1: [-1, -1, 2, 1, -1, -1].

title: Image Overlap
description:
You are given two images, `img1` and `img2`, represented as binary, square matrices of size `n x n`.

We translate one image however we choose (sliding it left, right, up, or down any number of units). An overlap is the number of positions that have a 1 in both images.

Return the largest possible overlap.

### Constraints
n == img1.length == img1[i].length
n == img2.length == img2[i].length
1 <= n <= 30
img1[i][j] is either 0 or 1.
img2[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

test_cases.explanation: Translate img1 right 1 and down 1 to overlap 3 ones.
Overlap is 1.

title: Minimum Non-Zero Product of the Array Elements
description:
You are given a positive integer `p`. Consider an array `nums` (1-indexed) that consists of the integers in the inclusive range `[1, 2^p - 1]` in their binary representations.

You can make any number of operations: pick two numbers `x` and `y` from `nums` and swap their bits at the same position.

Return the minimum non-zero product of `nums` modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
1 <= p <= 60

test_cases.explanation: nums = [1], non-zero product = 1.
nums = [1, 2, 3], minimum product after operations is 6.

title: Substring XOR Queries
description:
You are given a binary string `s`, and a 2D integer array `queries` where `queries[i] = [first_i, second_i]`.

For the `i`-th query, find the shortest substring of `s` whose decimal value `val` yields `val ^ first_i == second_i` (i.e. `val == first_i ^ second_i`). If multiple substrings exist, choose the one with minimum left index.

Return an array `ans` where `ans[i] = [left_i, right_i]` is the answer to the `i`-th query, or `[-1, -1]` if no such substring exists.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 10^4
s[i] is either '0' or '1'.
1 <= queries.length <= 10^5
0 <= first_i, second_i <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: Target 0^5 = 5 (bin '101') is at [0, 2]. Target 1^2 = 3 (bin '11') is at [2, 3].
Target 12^8 = 4 (bin '100') is not present in s, output [-1, -1].

title: Change Minimum Characters to Satisfy One of Three Conditions
description:
You are given two strings `a` and `b` that consist of lowercase English letters. In one operation, you can change any character in `a` or `b` to any other lowercase English letter.

Your goal is to satisfy one of the following three conditions with the minimum operations:
1. Every letter in `a` is strictly less than every letter in `b` in the alphabet.
2. Every letter in `b` is strictly less than every letter in `a` in the alphabet.
3. Both `a` and `b` consist of only one distinct letter.

Return the minimum number of operations needed.

### Constraints
2 <= a.length, b.length <= 10^5
a and b consist only of lowercase letters.

test_cases.explanation: Change b to 'ccc' with 2 operations to make all letters in a < all letters in b.
Change characters in 3 operations.

title: Stone Game VII
description:
Alice and Bob take turns playing a game, with Alice starting first.

There are `n` stones arranged in a row. On each turn, a player removes either the leftmost stone or the rightmost stone. The player's score increases by the sum of the values of the remaining stones.

Return the difference in Alice's score and Bob's score if they both play optimally.

### Constraints
1 <= values.length <= 1000
1 <= values[i] <= 1000

test_cases.explanation: Difference in score between Alice and Bob when both play optimally is 6.
Maximum score difference is 122.

title: Swap Adjacent in LR String
description:
In a string composed of 'L', 'R', and 'X' characters, a move consists of either replacing one occurrence of `"XL"` with `"LX"`, or replacing one occurrence of `"RX"` with `"XR"`.

Given the starting string `start` and the ending string `end`, return `true` if and only if there exists a sequence of moves to transform `start` into `end`.

### Constraints
1 <= start.length <= 10^4
start.length == end.length
Both start and end consist only of 'L', 'R', and 'X'.

test_cases.explanation: Valid sequence of 'XL' -> 'LX' and 'RX' -> 'XR' transforms start into end.
Cannot transform, return false.

title: Prime Palindrome
description:
Given an integer `n`, return the smallest prime palindrome greater than or equal to `n`.

An integer is prime if it has only two divisors: 1 and itself. An integer is a palindrome if it reads the same from left to right as it does from right to left.

### Constraints
1 <= n <= 10^8

test_cases.explanation: 7 is the smallest prime palindrome >= 6.
11 is the smallest prime palindrome >= 8.

title: Largest Sum of Averages
description:
You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. You can partition the array into at most `k` non-empty adjacent subarrays. The score of a partition is the sum of the averages of each subarray.

Return the maximum score you can achieve.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 100
1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
1 <= k <= nums.length

test_cases.explanation: Partition into [9], [1, 2, 3], [9]. Sum of averages = 9 + 2 + 9 = 20.0.
Maximum score is 20.5.

title: Minimum Absolute Sum Difference
description:
You are given two positive integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, both of length `n`.

The absolute sum difference is `sum(|nums1[i] - nums2[i]|)` for `0 <= i < n`.

You can replace at most one element of `nums1` with any other element from `nums1` to minimize the absolute sum difference.

Return the minimum absolute sum difference after replacing at most one element. Since the answer may be large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
n == nums1.length == nums2.length
1 <= n <= 10^5
1 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 10^5

test_cases.explanation: Both arrays are identical, minimum difference is 0.

title: Maximum Number of Consecutive Values You Can Make
description:
You are given an integer array `coins` of length `n` which represents the values of the `n` coins that you possess. The value of each coin is an integer.

You can make some value `x` if you can choose some of your coins such that their values sum up to `x`.

Return the maximum number of consecutive integer values that you can make with your coins starting from and including 0.

### Constraints
1 <= coins.length <= 4 * 10^4
1 <= coins[i] <= 4 * 10^4

test_cases.explanation: You can make values 0, 1, 3, 4 (2 consecutive values: 0, 1). Total consecutive = 2.
You can make 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, which gives 8 consecutive values.

title: Maximum Number of Eaten Apples
description:
There is a special kind of apple tree that grows apples every day for `n` days. On the `i`-th day, the tree grows `apples[i]` apples that will rot after `days[i]` days.

You can only eat at most one apple a day. You can continue eating apples even after the first `n` days.

Return the maximum number of apples you can eat.

### Constraints
n == apples.length == days.length
1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
0 <= apples[i], days[i] <= 2 * 10^4

test_cases.explanation: You can eat 7 apples across the days.
You can eat 5 apples.

title: Minimum Substring Partition of Equal Character Frequency
description:
Given a string `s`, you need to partition it into one or more balanced substrings. For example, in the string `"fabccddg"`, `"fabc"` is balanced since all of its characters appear once, and `"ccdd"` is balanced since both characters appear twice.

Return the minimum number of substrings needed to partition `s` such that every substring is balanced.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s consists only of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Partition into 'fabc', 'cd', 'dg'. Each partition has equal character frequencies. Total partitions = 3.
Minimum partitions is 2: 'abababa', 'ccddb' wait, 'abababaccddb' can be partitioned into 2 valid substrings.

title: Replace Question Marks in String to Minimize Its Value
description:
You are given a string `s`. `s[i]` is either a lowercase English letter or `'?'`.

For a string `t`, its value is the sum of the count of occurrences of each character in `t` before index `i` that are equal to `t[i]`.

Replace each `'?'` with a lowercase English letter such that the value of `s` is minimized. If there are multiple answers, return the lexicographically smallest one.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
s consists only of lowercase English letters and '?'.

test_cases.explanation: Greedily replace '?' to minimize value: 'abc'.
Replace with 'b' and 'c' -> 'abac'.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Satisfy Conditions
description:
You are given a 2D matrix `grid` of size `m x n`. In one operation, you can change the value of any cell to any digit from 0 to 9.

You want the resulting grid to satisfy the conditions:
- `grid[i][j] == grid[i + 1][j]` (all cells in the same column have the same value)
- `grid[i][j] != grid[i][j + 1]` (adjacent cells in the same row have different values)

Return the minimum number of operations needed.

### Constraints
m == grid.length
n == grid[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 1000
m * n <= 1000
0 <= grid[i][j] <= 9

test_cases.explanation: The grid already satisfies all conditions, 0 operations needed.
Requires 3 operations to satisfy conditions.

title: Reaching Points
description:
Given four integers `sx`, `sy`, `tx`, and `ty`, return `true` if it is possible to convert the point `(sx, sy)` to the point `(tx, ty)` through some operations, or `false` otherwise.

The allowed moves are:
- `(x, y) -> (x, x + y)`
- `(x, y) -> (x + y, y)`

### Constraints
1 <= sx, sy, tx, ty <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: Cannot reach (2, 2) from (1, 1), return false.

title: Nth Magical Number
description:
A positive integer is magical if it is divisible by either `a` or `b`.

Given the three integers `n`, `a`, and `b`, return the `n`-th magical number. Since the answer may be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
1 <= n <= 10^9
2 <= a, b <= 4 * 10^4

test_cases.explanation: The 1st magical number is 2.
Magical numbers: 2, 3, 4, 6. The 4th is 6.

title: Shortest Subarray With OR at Least K II
description:
You are given an array `nums` of non-negative integers and an integer `k`.

An array is called special if the bitwise OR of all of its elements is at least `k`.

Return the length of the shortest special non-empty subarray of `nums`, or return -1 if no special subarray exists.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^5
0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
0 <= k < 2^30

test_cases.explanation: Subarray [2] has bitwise OR 2 >= 2, length 1.
Subarray [2, 1, 8] has bitwise OR 11 >= 10, length 3.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint
description:
You are given a 0-indexed integer array `nums` and an integer `x`.

Find the minimum absolute difference between two elements in the array that are at least `x` indices apart. In other words, find `min(|nums[i] - nums[j]|)` such that `|i - j| >= x`.

Return the minimum absolute difference.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
0 <= x <= nums.length

title: Minimized Maximum of Products Distributed to Any Store
description:
You are given an integer `n` indicating there are `n` specialty retail stores. There are `m` product types of varying amounts, which are given as a 0-indexed integer array `quantities`, where `quantities[i]` represents the number of products of the `i`-th product type.

You need to distribute all products to the retail stores following these rules:
- A store can only be given at most one product type, but can be given any amount of it.
- After distribution, each store will have been given some number of products (possibly 0).

Return the minimum possible value of the maximum number of products given to any store.

### Constraints
1 <= n <= quantities.length <= 10^5
1 <= quantities[i] <= 10^5

test_cases.explanation: Distribute quantities to 6 stores with maximum products per store = 3.
Minimized maximum products is 5.

title: Campus Bikes II
description:
On a campus represented on an X-Y plane, there are `n` workers and `m` bikes, with `n <= m`.

You are given two 2D integer arrays `workers` and `bikes` representing their coordinates.

We assign one unique bike to each worker such that the sum of the Manhattan distances between each worker and their assigned bike is minimized.

Return the minimum possible sum of Manhattan distances.

### Constraints
n == workers.length
m == bikes.length
1 <= n <= m <= 10
workers[i].length == 2
bikes[i].length == 2
0 <= workers[i][j], bikes[i][j] < 1000

test_cases.explanation: Worker 0 gets bike 0 (dist 3), worker 1 gets bike 1 (dist 3). Total = 6.
Minimum total Manhattan distance is 4.

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence After at Most K Operations
description:
You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`.

In one operation, you can change any character in `s` to its preceding or succeeding character in the alphabet (wrapping around, so 'a' and 'z' are adjacent).

Return the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of `s` that can be obtained after at most `k` operations.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 200
1 <= k <= 200
s consists only of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Change 'd' to 'e' in 1 op and 'c' to 'e' in 2 ops to form 'abeee'. Subsequence 'eee' has length 3.
With at most 4 operations, maximum palindromic subsequence has length 6.

title: Mirror Reflection
description:
There is a special square room with mirrors on each of the four walls. Except for the southwest corner (where a laser starts at (0, 0)), there are receptors at the other three corners: (p, 0) is receptor 0, (p, p) is receptor 1, and (0, p) is receptor 2.

The laser ray emits from (0, 0) and meets the east wall at (p, q).

Return the number of the receptor that the ray meets first.

### Constraints
1 <= p <= 1000
0 <= q <= p

test_cases.explanation: Ray reflects to receptor 2 first.
Ray reflects to receptor 1.

title: Minimum Swaps to Arrange a Binary Grid
description:
Given an `n x n` binary grid, in one step you can choose two adjacent rows of the grid and swap them.

A grid is valid if all cells above the main diagonal are zeros.

Return the minimum number of steps needed to make the grid valid, or -1 if it is impossible.

### Constraints
n == grid.length == grid[i].length
1 <= n <= 200
grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1

test_cases.explanation: Row swaps bring grid to valid upper triangular form in 3 swaps.
Impossible to arrange, return -1.

title: Replace the Substring for Balanced String
description:
You are given a string `s` of length `n` containing only uppercase characters `'Q'`, `'W'`, `'E'`, and `'R'`.

A string is balanced if each of its characters appears `n / 4` times.

Return the minimum length of the substring that can be replaced with any other string of the same length to make `s` balanced.

### Constraints
n == s.length
4 <= n <= 10^5
n is a multiple of 4.
s contains only 'Q', 'W', 'E', and 'R'.

test_cases.explanation: The string is already balanced, return 0.
Replace 'Q' with 'R' (length 1) to make it balanced.

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted II
description:
You are given an array of `n` strings `strs`, all of the same length.

We may choose any deletion indices, and we delete all the characters in those indices for each string.

Return the minimum number of deletion indices needed such that the final array of strings is in lexicographic order (`strs[0] <= strs[1] <= ... <= strs[n - 1]`).

### Constraints
n == strs.length
1 <= n <= 100
1 <= strs[i].length <= 100
strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Delete column 0 to leave ['a','b','c'], which is sorted. Total deletes = 1.
The array is already sorted lexicographically, 0 deletions needed.

title: Smallest Integer Divisible by K
description:
Given a positive integer `k`, you need to find the length of the smallest positive integer `n` such that `n` is divisible by `k`, and `n` only contains the digit 1.

Return the length of `n`. If no such `n` exists, return -1.

### Constraints
1 <= k <= 10^5

test_cases.explanation: 1 is divisible by 1 (length 1).
No integer of only 1s is even, return -1.

title: Maximum Sum Obtained of Any Permutation
description:
We have an array of integers, `nums`, and an array of `requests` where `requests[i] = [start_i, end_i]`.

Return the maximum total sum of all requests among all permutations of `nums`. Since the answer may be too large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
0 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
1 <= requests.length <= 10^5
requests[i].length == 2
0 <= start_i <= end_i < nums.length

test_cases.explanation: Permutation [3, 5, 4, 2, 1] yields maximum request sum of 19.
Maximum sum is 11.

title: Maximum Points in an Archery Competition
description:
Alice and Bob are competing in an archery competition with 12 sections (0 to 11). Each section gives its index as points. To win section `k`, Bob must shoot strictly more arrows than Alice.

You are given the integer `numArrows` and integer array `aliceArrows`. Return the array of length 12 denoting the number of arrows Bob should shoot into each section to maximize his total score.

### Constraints
1 <= numArrows <= 10^5
aliceArrows.length == 12
sum(aliceArrows) == numArrows

test_cases.explanation: Bob wins sections with 27 points by optimal allocation of 9 arrows.
Bob wins section 11 with 33 points.

title: Split Two Strings to Make Palindrome
description:
You are given two strings `a` and `b` of the same length. Choose an index and split both strings at the same index, splitting `a` into `a_prefix` and `a_suffix`, and `b` into `b_prefix` and `b_suffix`.

Return `true` if `a_prefix + b_suffix` or `b_prefix + a_suffix` forms a palindrome, or `false` otherwise.

### Constraints
1 <= a.length, b.length <= 10^5
a.length == b.length
a and b consist of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Single characters are palindromes.
Split at index 3: 'x' + 'ecab' = 'xecab', or 'xb' + 'ab' = 'xbab' is not, but prefix of a with suffix of b forms 'x' + 'cab' wait, return false.

title: Find Valid Matrix Given Row and Column Sums
description:
You are given two arrays `rowSum` and `colSum` of non-negative integers where `rowSum[i]` is the sum of the elements in the `i`-th row and `colSum[j]` is the sum of the elements in the `j`-th column of a 2D matrix.

Find any non-negative 2D integer matrix of size `rowSum.length x colSum.length` that satisfies the row and column sums.

### Constraints
1 <= rowSum.length, colSum.length <= 500
0 <= rowSum[i], colSum[i] <= 10^8
sum(rowSum) == sum(colSum)

test_cases.explanation: Grid [[3, 0], [1, 7]] has row sums [3, 8] and col sums [4, 7].
Valid non-negative matrix constructed.

title: The Time When the Network Becomes Idle
description:
There is a network of `n` servers numbered from 0 to `n - 1`, where server 0 is the master server. You are given a 2D integer array `edges` and an integer array `patience`.

Each second, if a server has not received a reply, it sends another message every `patience[i]` seconds until it receives the original reply.

Return the earliest second starting from which the network becomes idle (no messages travelling in the network).

### Constraints
n == patience.length
2 <= n <= 10^5
patience[0] == 0
1 <= patience[i] <= 10^5 for 1 <= i < n
1 <= edges.length <= min(10^5, n * (n - 1) / 2)
edges[i].length == 2
0 <= ui, vi < n
ui != vi
There are no duplicate edges.
Each node is reachable from node 0.

test_cases.explanation: Network becomes idle at second 8.
Network becomes idle at second 3.

title: Can You Eat Your Favorite Candy on Your Favorite Day?
description:
You are given a 0-indexed array `candiesCount` where `candiesCount[i]` denotes the number of candies of the `i`-th type you have. You are also given a 2D integer array `queries` where `queries[i] = [favoriteType_i, favoriteDay_i, dailyCap_i]`.

You start eating candies on day 0, at most `dailyCap` candies per day, and cannot eat any candies of type `i` until all candies of type `i - 1` have been eaten.

Return a boolean array `answer` where `answer[i]` is `true` if you can eat at least one candy of type `favoriteType_i` on day `favoriteDay_i`.

### Constraints
1 <= candiesCount.length <= 10^5
1 <= candiesCount[i] <= 10^5
1 <= queries.length <= 10^5
queries[i].length == 3
0 <= favoriteType_i < candiesCount.length
0 <= favoriteDay_i <= 10^9
1 <= dailyCap_i <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: Answers to queries: [true, false, true].
Output: [false, true, true, false, false].

title: Count Number of Texts
description:
Alice is texting Bob using a phone keypad. Each digit maps to letters (keys 2-6 and 8 map to 3 letters, while 7 and 9 map to 4 letters).

Given a string `pressedKeys` representing the sequence of buttons pressed, return the total number of possible text messages Alice could have sent, modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
1 <= pressedKeys.length <= 10^5
pressedKeys only consists of digits from '2' - '9'.

test_cases.explanation: Possible text messages total 8.
Total possible texts modulo 10^9 + 7 is 82876089.

title: Cat and Mouse II
description:
A game is played by a cat and a mouse named Charlie and Pip on an `m x n` grid.

Pip starts at cell `M`, Charlie at `C`, and the food is at `F`. Charlie can jump up to `catJump` cells and Pip can jump up to `mouseJump` cells in 4 cardinal directions without jumping over walls `#`.

Pip wins if he gets to the food first. Charlie wins if he catches Pip or reaches food first. If 1000 turns pass, Charlie wins.

Return `true` if Pip wins assuming both play optimally, or `false` otherwise.

### Constraints
rows == grid.length
cols == grid[i].length
1 <= rows, cols <= 8
grid[i][j] consists only of 'C', 'M', 'F', '#', and '.'.
There is only one 'C', 'M', and 'F' in grid.
1 <= catJump, mouseJump <= 8

test_cases.explanation: Mouse can reach food before cat, return true.
Cat can catch the mouse, return false.

title: Maximize the Distance Between Points on a Square
description:
You are given an integer `side` representing the side length of a square whose corners are at `(0, 0)`, `(side, 0)`, `(side, side)`, and `(0, side)`.

You are also given a 2D integer array `points` where each `points[i] = [x_i, y_i]` lies on the boundary of the square, and an integer `k`.

You must select `k` points such that the minimum Manhattan distance between any two consecutively selected points along the boundary is maximized.

Return the maximum possible minimum distance.

### Constraints
1 <= side <= 10^9
4 <= points.length <= 15000
points[i].length == 2
0 <= xi, yi <= side
Each points[i] is guaranteed to lie on the perimeter of the square.
4 <= k <= min(points.length, 25)

test_cases.explanation: Selecting all 4 corners gives minimum distance between adjacent points = 2.
Maximum minimum distance is 2.

title: Minimum Sum of Values by Dividing Array
description:
You are given two arrays `nums` and `andValues` of length `n` and `m` respectively.

The value of a subarray is defined as the value of its last element.

You need to divide `nums` into `m` contiguous subarrays such that the bitwise AND of the `j`-th subarray equals `andValues[j]`.

Return the minimum possible sum of values of the `m` subarrays, or -1 if impossible.

### Constraints
1 <= n == nums.length <= 10^4
0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
1 <= m == andValues.length <= min(n, 10)
0 <= andValues[j] <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: Divide into [1,4], [3], [3], [2] with sum of last elements 4 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 12.

title: Maximum Score of Non-overlapping Intervals
description:
You are given a 2D integer array `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [l_i, r_i, weight_i]`.

You can choose at most 4 non-overlapping intervals such that the sum of their weights is maximized.

Return the lexicographically smallest list of indices of the chosen intervals that achieves the maximum weight.

### Constraints
1 <= intervals.length <= 4 * 10^4
intervals[i].length == 3
0 <= l_i <= r_i <= 10^9
1 <= weight_i <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: Choose intervals 2 and 3 with total weight 5 + 3 = 8.
Choose intervals 1 and 3 with weight 7 + 1 = 8.

title: Maximum Sum of Subsequence With Non-adjacent Elements
description:
You are given an array `nums` of integers and a 2D array `queries` where `queries[i] = [pos_i, x_i]`.

For each query, update `nums[pos_i] = x_i`, and find the maximum sum of a subsequence of `nums` such that no two elements in the subsequence are adjacent in the original array.

Return the sum of the answers to all queries modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 5 * 10^4
-10^5 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
1 <= queries.length <= 5 * 10^4
queries[i].length == 2
0 <= pos_i < nums.length
-10^5 <= x_i <= 10^5

test_cases.explanation: After query 0: nums = [3, -2, 9], max non-adjacent sum = 12. After query 1: nums = [-3, -2, 9], max sum = 9. Total = 21.
Max sum after query is 0.

title: Maximum Difference Between Even and Odd Frequency II
description:
You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`.

Find the maximum value of `freq(a) - freq(b)` over all substrings of `s` of length at least `k`, such that character `a` has an odd frequency and character `b` has a non-zero even frequency in the substring.

Return this maximum value, or -1 if no such substring exists.

### Constraints
3 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^4
s consists only of digits '0' to '4'.
1 <= k <= s.length

test_cases.explanation: In '12233', '1' has odd frequency 1, '2' has even frequency 2, difference is -1.
In '1122111', 1 appears 5 times, 2 appears 2 times. Difference = 5 - 2 = 3.

title: Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Substrings
description:
You are given a 0-indexed string `s` and you want to choose two non-overlapping palindromic substrings of odd length such that the product of their lengths is maximized.

Return the maximum possible product of the lengths of the two palindromic substrings.

### Constraints
2 <= s.length <= 10^5
s consists only of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Pick 'aba' (len 3) and 'aba' (len 3). Product = 9.
Pick 'aaa' (len 3) and 'bbb' (len 3). Product = 9.

title: Maximize Grid Happiness
description:
You are given four integers, `m`, `n`, `introvertsCount`, and `extrovertsCount`. You have an `m x n` grid, and there are two types of people: introverts and extroverts.

Introverts have initial happiness 120, and lose 30 happiness for each neighbor. Extroverts have initial happiness 40, and gain 20 happiness for each neighbor.

Return the maximum possible grid happiness.

### Constraints
1 <= m, n <= 5
1 <= m * n <= 25
0 <= introvertsCount, extrovertsCount <= min(m * n, 6)

test_cases.explanation: Maximum grid happiness achieved is 240.
Maximum grid happiness is 260.

title: Find the K-Sum of an Array
description:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`. You can choose any subsequence of the array and sum all of its elements together.

We define the K-Sum of the array as the `k`-th largest subsequence sum that can be generated (subsequences can be empty with sum 0).

Return the K-Sum of the array.

### Constraints
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
1 <= k <= min(2000, 2^n)

test_cases.explanation: The 5th largest subsequence sum is 2.
The 16th largest subsequence sum is 10.

title: Find the Minimum Cost Array Permutation
description:
You are given an array `nums` which is a permutation of `[0, 1, ..., n - 1]`.

The score of any permutation `perm` of `[0, 1, ..., n - 1]` is defined as:
`score(perm) = |perm[0] - nums[perm[1]]| + |perm[1] - nums[perm[2]]| + ... + |perm[n - 1] - nums[perm[0]]|`.

Return the lexicographically smallest permutation `perm` that achieves the minimum score.

### Constraints
2 <= nums.length <= 14
0 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
nums is a permutation of [0, 1, ..., nums.length - 1].

test_cases.explanation: Permutation [0, 1, 2] yields minimum score |0-0| + |1-2| + |2-1| = 2.
Permutation [0, 2, 1] yields score 2.

title: Make the XOR of All Segments Equal to Zero
description:
You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.

The XOR sum of all segments of length `k` should be equal to 0.

In one operation, you can change any element in `nums` to any integer in `[0, 1023]`.

Return the minimum number of elements to change.

### Constraints
1 <= k <= nums.length <= 2000
0 <= nums[i] < 2^10

test_cases.explanation: Modify 5 and 6 to 4 to make all 3-segments XOR to 0: 3 changes.
Change all non-zeros to 0: 3 operations.

title: Longest Substring of One Repeating Character
description:
You are given a 0-indexed string `s`. You are also given a string `queryCharacters` and an integer array `queryIndices`, both of length `k`.

For the `i`-th query, update `s[queryIndices[i]] = queryCharacters[i]`.

Return an array `ans` of length `k` where `ans[i]` is the length of the longest substring of `s` consisting of only one repeating character after the `i`-th query.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
s consists only of lowercase English letters.
1 <= characters.length == indices.length <= 10^5
characters[i] is a lowercase English letter.
0 <= indices[i] < s.length

test_cases.explanation: Updates yield longest repeating substring lengths [3, 3, 4].
Lengths are [2, 3].

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make String Sorted
description:
You are given a string `s` (0-indexed) consisting only of lowercase English letters. In one operation, you can apply the permutation algorithm step on `s` to produce the previous lexicographical permutation.

Return the number of operations needed to make `s` sorted in ascending order. Since the answer can be too large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
1 <= s.length <= 3000
s consists only of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: The sequence of operations will take 5 steps to sort 'cba' to 'abc'.
Takes 2 operations to sort 'aabaa'.

title: Count Number of Balanced Permutations
description:
You are given a string `num` of digits.

A permutation of digits is called balanced if the sum of the digits at even indices is equal to the sum of the digits at odd indices.

Return the number of distinct balanced permutations of `num` modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
num.length is even.
2 <= num.length <= 80
num consists only of digits from '0' to '9'.

test_cases.explanation: Balanced permutations are '132' and '231'. Total = 2.
Balanced permutation is '121'. Total = 1.

title: Delivering Boxes from Storage to Ports
description:
You have `n` boxes to deliver from storage to their respective ports. The `i`-th box has destination `boxes[i][0]` and weight `boxes[i][1]`. The ship can carry at most `maxBoxes` boxes and at most `maxWeight` total weight.

Moving between adjacent ports takes 1 trip, and returning to storage takes 1 trip.

Return the minimum number of trips to deliver all boxes in the given order.

### Constraints
1 <= boxes.length <= 10^5
1 <= portsCount, maxBoxes, maxWeight <= 10^5
boxes[i].length == 2
1 <= ports_i <= portsCount
1 <= weights_i <= maxWeight

test_cases.explanation: Storage -> Port 1 -> Port 2 -> Port 1 -> Storage = 4 trips.
Optimal loading requires 6 trips.

title: Least Operators to Express Number
description:
Given a single positive integer `x`, we can write an expression using the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, and `/` along with the number `x` to express `target`.

Return the least number of operators needed to express `target`.

### Constraints
1 <= x <= 100
1 <= target <= 2 * 10^8

test_cases.explanation: 3 * 3 + 3 * 3 + 3 / 3 = 19 uses 5 operators.

title: The Score of Students Solving Math Expression
description:
You are given a string `s` that contains digits 0-9 and operators `+` and `*`.

You are also given an integer array `answers` containing the answers submitted by students.

Students receive 5 points for the mathematically correct answer, and 2 points for an answer that could be obtained by incorrectly parenthesizing the expression.

Return the total score of all students.

### Constraints
3 <= s.length <= 31
s represents a valid expression that contains only digits 0-9, '+', and '*' without any leading zeros.
1 <= answers.length <= 10^4
0 <= answers[i] <= 1000

test_cases.explanation: Correct is 13 (5 pts). 20 is obtainable via (7+3)*1*2 (2 pts). Total = 7.
Score is 19.

title: Stamping The Sequence
description:
You are given two strings `stamp` and `target`. Initially, there is a string `s` of length `target.length` with all `'?'`.

In each turn, you may place `stamp` over `s` at any valid index and overwrite the corresponding characters.

Return an array of the index of the left-most letter being stamped at each turn to produce `target` from `s` within `10 * target.length` turns. If it is impossible, return an empty array.

### Constraints
1 <= stamp.length <= target.length <= 1000
stamp and target consist of lowercase English letters.

test_cases.explanation: Stamp at indices 0 then 2 gives 'ababc'.
Can stamp sequence to reach target.

title: Cat and Mouse
description:
A game is played on an undirected graph. Mouse starts at node 1, Cat starts at node 2, Hole is at node 0. Mouse moves first. Cat cannot enter the Hole (node 0).

If Mouse reaches Hole, Mouse wins (return 1). If Cat catches Mouse, Cat wins (return 2). If a position repeats, it is a Draw (return 0).

Return 1 if Mouse wins, 2 if Cat wins, or 0 if Draw assuming both play optimally.

### Constraints
3 <= graph.length <= 50
1 <= graph[i].length < graph.length
0 <= graph[i][j] < graph.length
graph[i][j] != i
graph[i] is strictly increasing.
The graph is undirected.

test_cases.explanation: Mouse can reach hole 0, returning 1.
Draw, return 0.

title: Maximum Total Beauty of the Gardens
description:
Alice is a caretaker of `n` gardens and she wants to plant flowers to maximize total beauty.

You are given an array `flowers` where `flowers[i]` is the number of flowers in garden `i`, and integers `newFlowers`, `target`, `full`, and `partial`.

A garden is complete if it has at least `target` flowers. The beauty is `(number of complete gardens) * full + (minimum flowers in any incomplete garden) * partial`.

Return the maximum beauty of the gardens Alice can achieve.

### Constraints
1 <= flowers.length <= 10^5
1 <= target <= 10^9
0 <= full, partial <= 10^6
1 <= newFlowers <= 10^14
1 <= flowers[i] <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: Add 5 flowers to make 1 complete garden, distribute remaining 2 flowers to get max beauty = 14.
Maximum total beauty is 30.

title: Maximum Number of Groups Getting Fresh Donuts
description:
There is a donut shop that bakes donuts in batches of `batchSize`. Each group `i` wants `groups[i]` donuts. A group gets fresh donuts if their order starts on an empty batch.

You can arrange the groups in any order.

Return the maximum number of groups that can get fresh donuts.

### Constraints
1 <= batchSize <= 9
1 <= groups.length <= 30
1 <= groups[i] <= 10^9

test_cases.explanation: 4 groups can receive fresh donuts by optimal ordering.
Maximum groups getting fresh donuts is 4.

title: Find the Sum of Subsequence Powers
description:
You are given an integer array `nums` of length `n`, and a positive integer `k`.

The power of a subsequence is defined as the minimum absolute difference between any two of its elements.

Return the sum of powers of all subsequences of `nums` of length `k`. Since the answer may be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

### Constraints
2 <= nums.length <= 50
-10^8 <= nums[i] <= 10^8
2 <= k <= nums.length

test_cases.explanation: All 4 subsequences of size 3 have power 1. Sum of powers = 4.
Subsequence [2, 2] has power 0.
